# no-multiple-space-closed-atx

- ID: `MD021`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `headings`, `atx_closed`, `spaces`

A closed heading has only one space inside each run of \#.

## Why

The extra spaces have no purpose, because they do not change the rendered
heading.

## Options

This rule has no options.

## Fix

The fix reduces each run of spaces to one. gomdlint may report a finding without
a fix when the fix would change a line with one character in brackets, such as
\[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add
or remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide #

##  Install  ##

Run the installer.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:4 Multiple spaces after opening hashes on closed ATX style heading
3:13 Multiple spaces before closing hashes on closed ATX style heading
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide #

## Install ##

Run the installer.
```

## Configure

Under `rules`, `no-multiple-space-closed-atx: false` turns the rule off and
`no-multiple-space-closed-atx: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-multiple-space-closed-atx` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-multiple-space-closed-atx -->
```
